meta.note: A snapshot of the Pokémon TCG card-image ecosystem. Links marked verified are pixel matches; the rest are the sites' own statements or indirect evidence. Not legal advice.

official.label: Official Pokémon
official.desc: The Pokémon Company, its regional companies and its game clients. The only true origin of digital card images.

extract.label: Game-client extract
extract.desc: Renders pulled out of the official game clients and re-published.

dataset.desc: A dump of an official source, published as a dataset.

rehost.desc: Card databases and APIs. Mostly re-host digital images from upstream sources.

wiki.desc: Community wikis. Modern cards re-hosted, vintage cards uploaded by users.

scan.desc: Images made by scanning or photographing physical cards. Owned by whoever scanned them.

tcgdex.label: TCGdex
tcgdex.desc: The open card database this atlas centres on.

print.label: Printed cards
print.desc: Physical cards. The origin of every scan and photo.

sources.name: Printed cards
sources.origin: Physical cards. The origin of every scan and photo. For Western cards from Base Set to Platinum (1999–2010), and Japanese cards before 2006, no official digital image was ever published online, so every picture of those cards is somebody's scan or photo. The only official digital versions we found are offline and small: Japan's 2005 Card Encyclopedia CD-ROM (162×226) and Wizards' redrawn Play It! cards.

sources.name: Pokémon Play It! (Wizards of the Coast, PC, 2000–01)
sources.eras: Base Set, Jungle, Fossil, some Team Rocket

api.note: Card images inside the game's Cards.pak archive

sources.origin: Wizards of the Coast's official PC card-game tutorial, released in several languages. Its cards are redrawn for the game: the official artwork on a newly typeset card layout, not the printed card. So they are not usable as card images, and they don't change the finding that Western 1999–2010 cards were never published as official digital card images. Checked in the French edition.

sources.name: Card Encyclopedia & Deck Builder (Japan, 2005 CD-ROM)

api.note: Preserved on the Internet Archive; card data in simple indexed tables

sources.origin: カードずかん & デッキビルダー, a Windows program on the CD-ROM of the Japanese Master Kit (2005). It holds every Japanese card released until then: 3,688 cards with name, reading, expansion, collection number, illustrator, promo source and holo flag, each with an official digital image. The images are clean print renders, not scans, but only 162×226. The only official digital images of Japanese 1996–2005 cards we found; too small to use as card images, but a complete official card list for that era.

sources.origin: Martin of Pokémon Paradijs scanned almost the entire English vintage era (Base Set → Platinum) in consistent, high quality. Remarkable work that deserves a credit wherever it's used.

sources.name: TCGdex

submissions.how: Images via the Ingest upload page (manager.tcgdex.net/ingest); card data via GitHub pull requests (CONTRIBUTING rejects AI-assisted data PRs)

terms.summary: Card data MIT-licensed. Image sources aren't listed per card. Takes image uploads through its Ingest page.

sources.origin: By pixel match: HGSS → Mega Evolution Pitch Black (me05) in every Western language is the exact same files as the game-client renders malie published (often months earlier). Pixels can't tell whether TCGdex took them from malie or from the game directly. The newest set, 30th Celebration (Sep 2026), is different: a differently cropped render that isn't malie's file and was online about 5 hours before malie's export, so it came from another source. English 1999–2010 is 94% the same files pokemontcg.io serves, i.e. Martin's Pokémon Paradijs scans; the rest (EX Dragon, EX FireRed & LeafGreen, parts of ex1/ex2/ex4) are 700×980 files that match no source we hold. French vintage: 43 of 96 sampled pre-HGSS images are the same files pkmcards.fr serves (from 0 of 10 in Base Set to 30 of 33 in the EX era), and 22 are pokemontcg.io's English files: 18 of 27 French POP-series images are the English scans. No German before HGSS. Sampled zh-cn images are the Traditional Chinese (Taiwan) print.

callouts.title: Korean: official images are watermarked
callouts.body: Pokémon Korea's official site (pokemoncard.co.kr) is the only digital source, and it serves only watermarked images. Every Korean fan database we found links to those same files. PriceCharting's Korean images are mostly photos of real cards (no watermark, but glare and texture), plus some official watermarked ones. No clean digital Korean image found anywhere (2010 → today).

callouts.title: Simplified Chinese: the full set only at 300×419
callouts.body: The only complete official source is Pokémon Shanghai's WeChat mini-program. Its images were scraped into the GitHub dataset duanxr/PTCG-CHS-Datasets at the app's native 300×419. Larger official renders (868×1212 and up) exist only for the 20–30 cards each product page on pokemon.cn highlights; 52poke has collected 1,328 of them (≈ 15% of the cards). AREAZERO.GG (tcg.mik.moe) shows the same 300×419 images as the dataset (pixel-identical in our sample) and no extra cards in the sets we compared; TCG Collector and PriceCharting carry the same renders for the cards we sampled. The dataset forbids redistribution without Pokémon Shanghai's written consent. Sampled TCGdex zh-cn images are the Traditional Chinese (Taiwan) print.

callouts.title: Better quality exists than TCGdex serves
callouts.body: TCGdex serves 600×825. malie's originals are 734×1024 with transparent corners; the Singapore English print on asia.pokemon-card.com is 744×1040; TCG Collector's Japanese scans reach 1280×1788; bisafans' German vintage photos are ≈ 860×1200; Poképédia's French vintage scans reach 1068 px wide; pokemon.cn's Simplified Chinese product renders are 868×1212 and up.

callouts.title: Western 1999–2010 has no official digital image
callouts.body: No Base Set → Platinum card was ever published as an official digital image online. Every image of those cards, TCGdex's included, is somebody's scan. For English, nearly everyone uses the same scans by Martin of Pokémon Paradijs. Japanese 1996–2006 is the same story online: the largest clean sets of scans we found are TCG Collector's and pcg-search.com's. Offline, the 2005 Card Encyclopedia CD-ROM has an official image of every Japanese card up to 2005, but only at 162×226.
